newsitem.title: USA: US lawmaker calls for water infrastructure funding.
newsitem.headline: US lawmaker calls for water infrastructure funding.

text.p: The federal government must continue to fund clean water infrastructure as it takes up reauthorization of the Clean Water Act, the chairman of a key U.S. House panel said on Tuesday.

"The backbone of any Clean Water Act reauthorization will continue to be investment in wastewater treatment infrastructure," Rep. Sherwood Boehlert, R-N.Y., chairman of the House water resources and environment subcommittee said.

Boehlert, who was speaking before the Association of Metropolitan Sewerage Agencies, said a recent Environmental Protection Agency survey estimates near-term wastewater infrastructure needs at about $137 billion.
And according to some estimates, over half of the 16,000 publicly owned treatment works now in operation discharge pollutants over their permitted levels, Boehlert said.
He added that in the next two decades an additional 1,750 public treatment works will be needed because of population and industrial growth.
"In order to make continued improvements in water quality and to preserve improvements we have already made, we must continue to invest in water infrastructure," he said.
Boehlert called reauthorization of the Clean Water Act a priority.
